text: The three days of travel may be read as a kind of suspended sentence. Nothing happens; everything happens. Item by item the narrator names the servants, the wood, the knife and the fire, and so sets down the instruments of the act before the act itself. Obedience and horror go forward together through those days, and neither is allowed to prevail; whatever faith Abraham has is shown in the measured road, and in the fire and the knife he carries in his hand.
